definition: A resistor is a passive component that opposes current flow and is commonly used to set currents, divide voltages, bias circuits, and terminate signals.
A variable resistor is a resistor whose resistance can be adjusted mechanically or electronically within a defined range.
A capacitor stores electric charge and is commonly used for filtering, decoupling, timing, coupling, and energy storage.
A polarized capacitor is a capacitor that must be connected with the specified terminal polarity to avoid incorrect operation or damage.
An inductor stores energy in a magnetic field and is commonly used in filtering, energy conversion, and impedance control.
A transformer transfers electrical energy between windings through magnetic coupling to change voltage, current, impedance, or isolation.
A ferrite bead is a frequency-dependent passive component used to impede high-frequency noise while passing lower-frequency or DC current.
A diode is a semiconductor component that primarily allows current in one direction and blocks it in the opposite direction within its ratings.
A rectifier diode is a diode optimized to conduct forward current and block reverse voltage in power-conversion applications.
A Zener diode is designed to operate in controlled reverse breakdown for voltage reference, limiting, or protection functions.
A transient-voltage-suppression diode is designed to clamp short overvoltage events and protect downstream circuitry.
A light-emitting diode is a polarized diode that emits light when forward biased within its electrical ratings.
A photodiode converts incident light into an electrical response for sensing and optical detection.
A fuse is an overcurrent protection component designed to open a circuit when current exceeds its rated behavior for sufficient time.
An NPN bipolar junction transistor is a three-terminal semiconductor device in which base current controls a larger collector-to-emitter current.
A PNP bipolar junction transistor is a three-terminal semiconductor device in which base drive controls current in the complementary polarity to an NPN device.
An N-channel MOSFET is a voltage-controlled transistor that uses an electric field at the gate to control current through an N-type channel.
A P-channel MOSFET is a voltage-controlled transistor that controls current through a P-type channel and is commonly used for high-side or complementary switching.
An operational amplifier is a high-gain differential amplifier commonly used with feedback for analog amplification, filtering, buffering, and signal conditioning.
A comparator is an analog circuit that changes its output state according to which of two input voltages is greater.
A battery is an electrochemical source that supplies DC electrical energy within specified voltage, current, capacity, and temperature limits.
A voltage regulator maintains an output voltage within a specified range despite allowed changes in input voltage and load.
A linear regulator controls output voltage by dissipating excess input voltage as heat while operating in its regulation range.
A switching regulator converts electrical power by rapidly switching energy-storage elements to achieve efficient voltage conversion.
A power module is an integrated assembly that combines power-conversion components into a defined electrical and mechanical interface.
A NOT gate produces the opposite digital logic state of its input after the specified propagation delay.
An AND gate produces a high output only when all required inputs are high under the simulator's logic rules.
An OR gate produces a high output when at least one required input is high under the simulator's logic rules.
A NAND gate produces the logical inverse of an AND operation.
A NOR gate produces the logical inverse of an OR operation.
An XOR gate produces a high output when its relevant binary inputs differ according to the implemented logic convention.
An XNOR gate produces the logical inverse of an XOR operation.
A flip-flop is a digital storage element that holds one bit of state according to its clocking and control behavior.
A microcontroller is an integrated circuit that combines a processor core with memory and peripherals for embedded control tasks.
A processor is a programmable integrated circuit that executes instructions to perform computation and control functions.
A memory device stores digital information using a defined technology, interface, capacity, and timing specification.
An application-specific integrated circuit is a chip designed to perform a specialized set of functions rather than general-purpose computing.
A temperature sensor converts temperature into an electrical or digital signal according to its specified range and accuracy.
A current sensor measures electrical current and produces a corresponding analog or digital output.
A light sensor measures incident light and produces an electrical or digital response.
A crystal resonator uses piezoelectric resonance to provide a stable frequency reference when used in a suitable circuit.
An oscillator generates a periodic signal at a defined nominal frequency and electrical interface.
A connector provides a detachable or permanent electrical interface between a PCB and another circuit, cable, board, or device.
A switch mechanically or electronically changes the conductive state between defined terminals.
A relay uses an electrical control signal to open or close electrically isolated or separately rated contacts.
A test point is an intentionally accessible electrical connection used for measurement, debugging, programming, or production test.
A display is an output component that presents visual information through segments, pixels, characters, or another defined interface.
A buzzer is an electrically driven component that produces audible sound when energized with an appropriate signal.
A motor converts electrical energy into mechanical rotation or motion within its drive and load ratings.
A mounting hole is a mechanical board feature used for fastening or alignment and is not automatically an electrical component.
